sentence_level_traceability.spoken_text: Google's next AI test bed isn't on Earth.

verified_facts.statement: Project Suncatcher exists as a legitimate Google research initiative exploring space-based AI computing.
verified_facts.supporting_context: Google Research publicly unveiled 'Project Suncatcher', a research initiative exploring the physical and architectural feasibility of deploying machine learning accelerators in low Earth orbit.

verified_facts.statement: Project Suncatcher is an exploratory research and experimental project rather than a commercial product or operational data center.
verified_facts.supporting_context: Project Suncatcher is a long-term research moonshot investigating hardware resilience, thermal constraints, and communication architectures in space; it is not a commercial service.

sentence_level_traceability.editorial_audit_notes: Opening hook accurately categorizes the initiative as an 'AI test bed' rather than an operational system. Traceability to claim-01 and claim-02 is verified. Note on-screen text 'AI TEST BED IN ORBIT' has potential minor temporal ambiguity since launch has not occurred (scheduled Oct 1, 2026); recommend adjusting to 'ORBITAL AI TEST BED' or 'AI TEST BED HEADED TO ORBIT'.

sentence_level_traceability.spoken_text: Project Suncatcher is a research prototype testing if AI chips can run in orbit.

verified_facts.statement: Google plans to test its proprietary Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) hardware in low Earth orbit.
verified_facts.supporting_context: Google plans to operate datacenter-class TPUs in orbit to gather empirical data on microgravity, vacuum operation, and radiation tolerance during live AI inference.

verified_facts.statement: Project Suncatcher is already an operational orbital AI data center.
verified_facts.supporting_context: Project Suncatcher is an early-stage prototype testbed (MVP) scheduled for a first launch on October 1, 2026. It is not an operational data center, does not serve customer workloads, and consists of a single experimental test satellite.

sentence_level_traceability.editorial_audit_notes: Exemplary adherence to prototype integrity guardrails. Explicitly terms the hardware a 'research prototype' and reinforces claim-19 refutation on screen.

sentence_level_traceability.spoken_text: Built with Planet Labs, this compact satellite carries four Trillium TPUs and a one-kilowatt solar array.

verified_facts.statement: Earth-imaging company Planet Labs (Planet) is partnering with Google and built the prototype spacecraft.
verified_facts.supporting_context: Google partnered with Planet Labs, leveraging Planet's agile satellite bus architecture to manufacture and host the MVP prototype spacecraft.

verified_facts.statement: The prototype satellite carries four TPUs.
verified_facts.supporting_context: The MVP satellite payload is equipped with four TPUs, structured analogously to a 4-chip compute block.

verified_facts.statement: The prototype satellite carries Google's sixth-generation Trillium TPUs (TPU v6e).
verified_facts.supporting_context: The chips installed in the MVP spacecraft are Google's latest sixth-generation Trillium TPUs (TPU v6e), built for energy-efficient matrix multiplication and ML inference.

verified_facts.statement: All specific numerical claims in the candidate entry (1kW solar array, 4 TPUs, etc.) are accurate.
verified_facts.supporting_context: Every numerical metric in the candidate record is verified: 1 kilowatt solar power, 4 Trillium TPUs.

sentence_level_traceability.editorial_audit_notes: Hardware details fully verified. Remediated: On-screen text card aligned to 6 words ('4 TRILLIUM TPUs • 1 kW ARRAY'), strictly complying with QA Gate 09.

sentence_level_traceability.spoken_text: In a dawn-dusk orbit, panels can capture up to eight times more solar energy annually than on Earth.

verified_facts.statement: Dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit enables nearly continuous solar power generation.
verified_facts.supporting_context: Satellites in a dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit travel along the terminator line, maintaining near-constant visibility of the Sun without entering Earth's shadow.

verified_facts.statement: Space-based solar panels can yield up to 8x the annual energy productivity of terrestrial solar panels.
verified_facts.supporting_context: Google Research calculated that solar panels in a dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit generate up to 8x more electrical energy per year than identical panels at mid-latitudes on Earth.

sentence_level_traceability.editorial_audit_notes: REMEDIATED (Phase 5R): Master script, visual direction, and storyboard synchronized to qualified dawn-dusk orbit phrasing ('In a dawn-dusk orbit, panels can capture up to eight times more solar energy annually than on Earth.'). Primary on-screen text card updated to 'UP TO 8× ANNUAL SOLAR HARVEST' (5 words), adhering strictly to QA Gate 04 (no permanent 100% illumination claims) and QA Gate 09 (<= 6 words limit).

sentence_level_traceability.spoken_text: The catch? A vacuum has no air for cooling, and space radiation triggers memory bit-flips.
sentence_level_traceability.on_screen_text: VACUUM HEAT TRAP • NO CONVECTION / RADIATION SINGLE-EVENT BIT-FLIP

verified_facts.statement: Google conducted extensive pre-launch radiation testing on Trillium TPUs at the Crocker Nuclear Laboratory.
verified_facts.supporting_context: Engineers evaluated active Trillium TPUs using a cyclotron proton beam at UC Davis Crocker Nuclear Laboratory, validating survival past 15 krad(Si) against a 750 rad(Si) 5-year mission requirement.

verified_facts.statement: Cosmic radiation induces single-event bit-flips and silent data corruption in orbital TPUs.
verified_facts.supporting_context: Beam experiments showed high-energy protons triggered Single-Event Upsets (SEUs) and occasional silent data corruption, with High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) proving most sensitive.

verified_facts.statement: Operating compute accelerators in space faces severe vacuum thermal dissipation challenges.
verified_facts.supporting_context: The vacuum of space eliminates convective airflow cooling, requiring all heat generated by high-power TPUs to be managed strictly through conduction and radiation.

primary_source.name: UC Davis Crocker Nuclear Laboratory / Google Research

sentence_level_traceability.editorial_audit_notes: Mechanisms are scientifically sound and accurately trace to primary radiation and thermodynamic tests. Zero convective fans depicted; binary SEU (0->1 bit flip) accurately rendered without sci-fi explosions.

sentence_level_traceability.spoken_text: Using heat pipes and radiators, it runs fifteen-minute bursts, preparing to launch October first on SpaceX.

verified_facts.statement: The prototype satellite is scheduled to launch aboard SpaceX Falcon 9 Transporter-18.
verified_facts.supporting_context: The prototype satellite payload is integrated onto SpaceX's Transporter-18 dedicated rideshare mission lifting off from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

verified_facts.statement: The prototype launch is scheduled for October 1, 2026 (the satellite has not yet launched).
verified_facts.supporting_context: The launch is targeted for October 1, 2026. As of today, September 26, 2026, the satellite remains on the ground undergoing pre-flight checkout.

verified_facts.statement: The prototype satellite employs conductive heat pipes to move heat away from the TPUs.
verified_facts.supporting_context: A network of sealed conductive heat pipes with thermal interface materials transfers heat from the TPU chip dies to the external spacecraft structure.

verified_facts.statement: External radiators reject thermal energy into deep space, constraining operations to 15-minute bursts.
verified_facts.supporting_context: Exterior radiator surfaces radiate heat away as infrared radiation into space. Because radiative cooling is slow, the MVP runs AI workloads in ~15-minute bursts followed by cooling cycles.

verified_facts.statement: All specific numerical claims (15-min bursts, Oct 1 launch) verified.
verified_facts.supporting_context: Confirmed 15-minute burst duty cycle and October 1, 2026 launch date.

sentence_level_traceability.editorial_audit_notes: Temporal accuracy strictly respected ('preparing to launch October first on SpaceX'). Passive conductive and radiative cooling mechanisms accurately stated alongside 15-minute burst operational duty cycle.

sentence_level_traceability.spoken_text: If proven, orbital compute could eventually bypass Earth's strained power grids.

verified_facts.statement: The long-term vision incorporates free-space optical (laser) inter-satellite links.
verified_facts.supporting_context: Google's architecture envisions interconnected constellations communicating via high-bandwidth laser cross-links, forming a distributed orbital mesh network.

sentence_level_traceability.editorial_audit_notes: Properly phrased as an aspirational conditional future ('If proven... could eventually bypass'), avoiding misleading claims of immediate replacement. Storyboard Shot 08 correctly marks this visual state with a prominent 'FUTURE CONCEPT' watermark.
